payload.reason: The evidence provides a clear description of how crowd workers were instructed to identify important elements in large document collections through a novel crowdsourcing scheme called low-context importance annotation.

claims.text: Crowd workers were instructed to identify important elements in document collections using a new crowdsourcing scheme called low-context importance annotation, which allows them to determine importance without reading all documents.
The low-context importance annotation scheme simplifies the task for workers, making it more efficient and scalable by not requiring them to read all documents in a cluster.
Workers provided Likert-scores for propositions to determine their importance, which were then used to rank the most important propositions through pairwise comparisons.
